_meta.purpose: Seed data for future mapping into the app's MarketOpportunity object (lib/types.ts). Not wired into lib/mock/data.ts or any app code. Research-only, per issue #4.
_meta.IMPORTANT_deviation_from_lib_types_ts: lib/types.ts's MarketOpportunity uses numeric demandScore/capabilityScore/competitionScore/marginPotentialPct fields. Per issue #4's explicit 'do not fabricate volumes or market sizes' guardrail, this seed data deliberately uses qualitative tiers (low/medium/high) plus a rationale string instead of fabricated precise numbers. A human or a follow-up pass with real data (keyword volumes, pricing research) should define and document an explicit, defensible tier-to-number mapping before these are converted to the app's numeric fields -- do not silently assign e.g. low=33/medium=66/high=100 without that documented step.
_meta.geographyNote: Every record covers both US and AU per the issue's scope, but see geographySignal for where part-type-level evidence was actually found vs. only market/policy-level evidence (AU). See README.md executive summary.

marketOpportunities.name: Actuator & Joint Housings
marketOpportunities.description: Custom precision housings for linear/rotary actuators and harmonic-drive/gearbox joints in robot arms, cobots, and (per 2026 supply-chain coverage) humanoid robots.
marketOpportunities.demandTierRationale: Multiple dedicated US supplier landing pages for this exact part type, plus a documented 2026 humanoid-robotics supply-chain bottleneck specifically naming precision actuator/gearbox components as constrained -- a real demand tailwind, but no measured order volume for our own funnel exists.
marketOpportunities.capabilityTierRationale: Manufacturing OS has not yet onboarded or profiled any supplier network; declared/observed supplier capability for this part type is not yet assessed. Not to be confused with market demand -- this is Manufacturing OS's own supply-side readiness, which this research did not investigate.
marketOpportunities.competitionTierRationale: At least 4 distinct competitor types found: generalist instant-quote marketplaces, robotics-specialist job shops with dedicated landing pages, humanoid-joint-specific technical-content-led competitors, and overseas (China-based) manufacturers targeting the identical keyword space.
marketOpportunities.marginPotentialNote: No pricing data collected for this cluster; not assessable from this research pass.
marketOpportunities.riskNote: High technical precision requirement (backlash/preload control) raises quality/rework risk for a new entrant; humanoid-driven demand growth is a real but unproven tailwind for Manufacturing OS specifically.

evidence.summary: See actuator-housings.md for full per-claim citations; this record synthesizes across that file.

marketOpportunities.name: Gripper Jaws / Components & EOAT
marketOpportunities.description: Custom gripper jaws, fingers, drive/coupling components, and end-of-arm-tooling plates for pick-and-place, palletizing, grinding, and assembly applications.
marketOpportunities.demandTierRationale: Real organic buyer discovery behavior evidenced by a forum thread asking 'who makes' a specific gripper design; existence of a public third-party EOAT price guide implies real, cost-conscious buyer comparison shopping; multiple dedicated US supplier landing pages.
marketOpportunities.capabilityTierRationale: Not yet assessed -- see actuator/joint housing record note.
marketOpportunities.competitionTierRationale: Dedicated specialists on both the machining side (RivCut, Zintilon) and the additive-manufacturing side (ANUBIS 3D, Forerunner3D), plus generalist marketplaces -- a crowded, two-process-family competitive field.
marketOpportunities.marginPotentialNote: Only cost data found: secondary source states $200-$1,000 for entry-level EOAT, $1,000-$3,000 for mid-range -- single source, not independently corroborated, and price is not margin.
marketOpportunities.riskNote: Grip-surface tolerance is explicitly the highest-precision feature; quality risk on a single tight-tolerance feature per part.

evidence.summary: See gripper-jaws-eoat.md for full per-claim citations; this record synthesizes across that file.

marketOpportunities.name: Sensor & Camera Mounts
marketOpportunities.description: Vibration-isolating, precisely aligned mounts for machine-vision cameras, encoders, LiDAR, and force sensors.
marketOpportunities.demandTierRationale: Real dedicated competitor pages exist (Frigate, RivCut, Zintilon, CNCTAL, Met3DP) but the coexistence of commodity/off-the-shelf mount sellers (RobotShop, Ruland) suggests a meaningful share of this segment is served by non-custom parts, capping how much of the visible demand is truly custom-manufacturing demand.
marketOpportunities.capabilityTierRationale: Not yet assessed -- see actuator/joint housing record note.
marketOpportunities.competitionTierRationale: Fewer dedicated specialists than gripper/EOAT or actuator housings; one 2026-dated additive-manufacturing-specific competitor found (Met3DP), suggesting the field is still forming around process choice.
marketOpportunities.marginPotentialNote: No pricing data collected; not assessable.
marketOpportunities.riskNote: Lower structural-precision demands than joint housings; primary risk is optical/alignment tolerance rather than load-bearing failure.

evidence.summary: See sensor-camera-mounts.md for full per-claim citations; this record synthesizes across that file.

marketOpportunities.name: Motor Mounts & Adapter/Base Plates
marketOpportunities.description: Precision motor/gearbox mounting plates and robot-to-tool adapter plates bridging heterogeneous bolt patterns, with a notable cobot-specific sub-segment.
marketOpportunities.demandTierRationale: Real dedicated product lines exist (Trimantec, EMI Corp, MS Machining) but fewer independent sources were found overall for this cluster than for gripper/EOAT or actuator housings, and the existence of 'blank plate' self-machined SKUs suggests some of this demand is absorbed by DIY/semi-custom purchase paths rather than fully custom manufacturing.
marketOpportunities.capabilityTierRationale: Not yet assessed -- see actuator/joint housing record note.
marketOpportunities.competitionTierRationale: Several dedicated vendors found but the segment appears less consolidated/marketed than gripper or actuator housings.
marketOpportunities.marginPotentialNote: No pricing data collected; not assessable.
marketOpportunities.riskNote: Primarily a bolt-pattern-matching/interoperability problem rather than a high-precision manufacturing problem; likely lower technical risk than joint housings or gripper grip surfaces.

evidence.summary: See motor-mounts-adapter-plates.md for full per-claim citations; this record synthesizes across that file.

marketOpportunities.name: Structural Brackets & Enclosures
marketOpportunities.description: Custom sheet-metal enclosures and structural brackets for robot-cell electronics housing and safety guarding, typically specified to a named IP rating.
marketOpportunities.demandTierRationale: A regulatory/compliance-driven sub-segment (safety enclosures) exists alongside a general electronics-housing sub-segment; multiple dedicated vendors including at least one (Vention) that is a broader automation-hardware platform, and one overseas (China-based) OEM/ODM competitor.
marketOpportunities.capabilityTierRationale: Not yet assessed -- see actuator/joint housing record note.
marketOpportunities.competitionTierRationale: Distinct from milling-centric clusters -- this segment's primary process (sheet metal fab) is served by both robotics-specific vendors and the broader general sheet-metal-fabrication marketplace field (see cnc-sheet-metal-general.md).
marketOpportunities.marginPotentialNote: No pricing data collected; not assessable.
marketOpportunities.riskNote: IP-rating compliance is a clear, checkable spec (lower ambiguity risk than a bespoke precision-tolerance part), but safety-enclosure applications may carry liability/compliance considerations worth flagging to the human reviewer.

evidence.summary: See structural-brackets-enclosures.md for full per-claim citations; this record synthesizes across that file.

marketOpportunities.name: Jigs, Fixtures & Inspection Fixtures
marketOpportunities.description: Custom machining, welding, assembly, check, and CMM-inspection fixtures, often built as turnkey tooling tied to a specific production line or robot cell.
marketOpportunities.demandTierRationale: This is the one cluster where generalist instant-quote marketplaces appear comparatively absent as named competitors (no source found them marketing 'fixtures' as a dedicated category), while dedicated US specialists are numerous -- suggesting real, durable, specialist-served demand that a generalist marketplace model may not currently capture well.
marketOpportunities.capabilityTierRationale: Not yet assessed -- see actuator/joint housing record note.
marketOpportunities.competitionTierRationale: Numerous US specialists (Mahuta Tool, MD Design & Automation, KTM Solutions, CAVTool, PJF Inc., Yicen Precision) but comparatively little generalist-marketplace competition, per demandTierRationale.
marketOpportunities.marginPotentialNote: No pricing data collected; not assessable.
marketOpportunities.riskNote: Design-through-build-through-metrology is framed as one coupled service by every specialist found, meaning a pure fabrication-only offering (upload-a-drawing, get-a-part) may be a weaker fit for this cluster than for the other, more drawing-driven part types -- worth flagging for the human reviewer as a possible product-fit gap.

evidence.summary: See jigs-fixtures-inspection.md for full per-claim citations; this record synthesizes across that file.

marketOpportunities.name: General Custom CNC / Sheet-Metal Parts
marketOpportunities.description: The broad, generalist custom-machined and sheet-metal-part category that every other cluster above must also compete within, dominated by large multi-process instant-quote marketplaces.
marketOpportunities.demandTierRationale: Largest and most mature competitor set found in this entire research pass (at least 8 distinct multi-process marketplaces plus multiple Australia-specific instant-quote providers); IFR/A3-reported robot-install-base and order growth in the US, and Australia's National Robotics Strategy and market-research forecasts, both support a real and growing underlying industrial-automation buyer base this category serves, though none of these figures measure this category's demand directly.
marketOpportunities.capabilityTierRationale: Not yet assessed -- see actuator/joint housing record note.
marketOpportunities.competitionTierRationale: This is the most saturated, best-capitalized competitive field in the wedge (Xometry, Protolabs Network, Fictiv, RapidDirect, PCBWay, JLCCNC, PartsBadger, Geomiq globally; Zeal 3D, Precision Manufacturing Australia, Berkeley Engineering, Elite CNC, Xometry AU/NZ in Australia).
marketOpportunities.marginPotentialNote: No pricing data collected; not assessable. High competition among well-capitalized generalists plausibly compresses margin on undifferentiated SKUs, but this is inference, not measured.
marketOpportunities.riskNote: Highest competitive-intensity risk in the wedge; Manufacturing OS's differentiation must come from the robotics-specific ontology/evidence model (per docs/product/PRODUCT.md), not from competing as a generic instant-quote marketplace.

evidence.summary: See cnc-sheet-metal-general.md for full per-claim citations; this record synthesizes across that file.
